concepts.title: Remote Sensing: Concept, Stages and Platforms
concepts.definition: Remote sensing is the science of acquiring information about the earth's surface without physical contact, using electromagnetic energy through stages of energy source, interaction with the target, recording by sensors on platforms like aircraft and satellites, transmission, processing and interpretation into images and maps.
concepts.textbook_ref: Sensors record reflected sunlight in the visible and infrared bands or emit their own microwave energy, giving passive and active systems like radar.

concepts.title: Indian Remote Sensing Satellites and Applications
concepts.definition: India's IRS satellite series launched by ISRO supplies images used in agriculture, forestry, water resources, land use, drought and flood monitoring, and multispectral digital data processed into false colour composites lets interpreters identify features by their spectral signatures.
concepts.textbook_ref: False colour composite images show vegetation in red, and the digital data support computer classification and GIS integration for planning.

concepts.title: Electromagnetic Radiation and Interaction with Targets
concepts.definition: Remote sensing uses electromagnetic radiation ranging from visible light to infrared and microwave, and each surface target reflects or emits this energy differently by wavelength, so the interaction of radiation with water, vegetation and soil produces the spectral differences that sensors record.
concepts.key_idea: Healthy vegetation reflects strongly in the near infrared while water absorbs almost all radiation, which is why spectral bands are chosen for each application.
